newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Dec 16.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on December 16. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Four people were killed and six injured when a severe storm swept through Jakarta on Sunday afternoon.
Two Singaporeans have been arrested while trying to smuggle 16,527 Ecstasy pills into Indonesia.

Indonesia says it has no intention of upgrading the regular South China Sea workshops it hosts into an inter-governmental forum on the territorial disputes over a number disputed islands in that region.
Rudini, a former Interior Minister, has said widespread violence in Indonesia is caused by the government's heavy-handed approach in handling socio-political problems.

More than 100,000 members of the Moslem socio-cultural group Nahdlatul Ulama gathered at a stadium in Surabaya on Sunday to celebrate the group's founding as well as prayer for the safety of next year's general elections and the national leadership.
Car industry observers predict Indonesian vehicle production will increase by 15 percent in 1997.

Budiman Sudjatmiko, leader of the left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) whose leaders are being tried on subversion charges, has said in an interview that his group is not communist or atheist and is like the old Indonesian Socialist Party (PSI).
